newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Monday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower amid outlooks for soft pork prices next week, livestock dealers said. Prices also could be pressured by projections for increased hog supplies, they said.
Hog supplies reportedly were starting a seasonal increase that several market sources said could extend into the winter.
Pork production for the week ended Saturday, August 16, was estimated at 312.9 million pounds, up 1.2 percent from a week ago, USDA reported on Friday.
The increase in pork supplies was seen weighing on wholesale pork prices next week, the market sources said.

Fresh pork loin prices at midday Friday were not fully established with a weak tone, hams and bellies were steady, and lean trimmings were quoted $3.00 per cwt lower, USDA said in its central U.S. carlot pork report.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs at the plant were seen steady with Friday at $57.50. Illinois top hog prices delivered to the plant were seen steady at $56.50 and Indiana/Ohio top plant hog prices were expected at $56.50 to $57.00.
